# The Stars That Shed Their Light

## Scripture

**"The heavens declare the glory of God; the skies proclaim the work of his hands. Day after day they pour forth speech; night after night they reveal knowledge."** — Psalm 19:1–2

## Reflection

On a clear October night, if you find a dark enough spot away from city lights, you may notice something remarkable: the Andromeda Galaxy. It sits 2.5 million light-years away, yet it is visible to the naked eye—a faint, soft smudge of ancient light. The photons reaching your eyes tonight began their journey before humanity existed. They have been traveling, unbroken, across an ocean of space, simply to arrive here and now, at this moment, for you.

The psalmist says the heavens "pour forth speech." Not a shout—a pour. A steady, patient streaming of light that has never stopped. Creation does not merely point to God; it *pours* Him out, day after day, night after night, generation after generation. The same light that reached Abraham, that guided shepherds to Bethlehem, reaches us still.

Fall reminds us that light persists even as seasons change. The days shorten, but the stars do not dim. When your own faith feels like a faint smudge against a vast darkness, remember: God's glory has been traveling toward you longer than you can imagine. It will not fail to arrive. You are not forgotten by the light.

## Prayer

Father of lights, thank You for the ancient beams that find us still. When my faith feels faint, remind me that Your glory has been pouring out since before time began—and it reaches me tonight. Let me be a small, steady light for others, traveling faithfully until it lands. In Jesus' name, Amen.
